title: Portuguese (Portugal)
description: Learn European Portuguese as spoken in Portugal: greetings, numbers, food, family and travel.

units.title: Greetings
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
tips: Men say 'obrigado' and women say 'obrigada'. Both mean 'thank you'.

units.title: Introductions
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
tips: In Portugal the pronoun usually goes after the verb with a hyphen: 'Chamo-me Ana' (My name is Ana).

units.title: Being polite
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
tips: 'Percebo' (I understand) is very common in Portugal; 'compreendo' and 'entendo' are also correct.

units.title: Numbers 1–10
units.description: Numbers, food and drink, and talking about your family.
tips: 'Um' and 'dois' change for feminine nouns: 'uma maçã', 'duas maçãs'.

units.title: Food and drink
units.description: Numbers, food and drink, and talking about your family.
tips: In Portugal, breakfast is 'o pequeno-almoço' and a short espresso is often called 'uma bica' in Lisbon.

units.title: Family
units.description: Numbers, food and drink, and talking about your family.
tips: In Portugal the article usually comes before possessives: 'a minha mãe' (my mother), 'o meu pai' (my father).

units.title: Getting around
units.description: Travel basics, ordering at a café, and days of the week.
tips: European Portuguese has its own travel words: a train is 'o comboio' and a bus is 'o autocarro'.

units.title: At the café
units.description: Travel basics, ordering at a café, and days of the week.
tips: 'Queria' (I would like) is a polite way to order in Portugal. A menu is 'a ementa'.

phrases.e: I would like a tea with milk.

units.title: Days and time
units.description: Travel basics, ordering at a café, and days of the week.
tips: Weekdays are numbered: 'segunda-feira' is Monday (the 'second day'). People often shorten them: 'segunda', 'terça'…
